condition: exertional hyperthermia on hot factory floor with heavy sweating dizzy spell and 105 F oral temperature
level_rationale: A 42-year-old factory worker who worked 4 hours on a hot factory floor today, sweated heavily, had a brief dizzy spell, and has an oral temperature of 105 F (40.6 C) has dangerous exertional hyperthermia at immediate risk of heatstroke organ injury requiring emergency hospital cooling and evaluation, whereas the exact same post-shift heavy sweating and brief transient dizzy spell with a normal 97 F oral temperature leaves no hyperthermia or neurologic red flag and is suitable for cool-room rest and oral fluid self-care.

everyday_sources.evidence: A 73-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a syncopal episode and a history of dizzy spells.
everyday_sources.adaptation: Singularized plural 'dizzy spells' to 'dizzy spell' for a single acute episode in a US patient report.

lexicon_entries: spell (a shaking spell, a fainting spell, a dizzy spell)

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: US colloquial core lexicon swap ('episode of dizziness' vs 'dizzy spell', retained in everyday_paraphrase and changed_fact) + single-fact measured oral temperature de-escalation control (-cf, 105 F to 97 F, L4 to L1).

design_note: Structures f1..f3 as heat exposure, heavy sweating, and one brief dizzy spell with the hyperthermic emergency isolated to measured oral temperature fact f4 ('is 105 F'). Changing only the oral temperature to 'is 97 F' follows Rule A's first-choice measured-value control design with zero stranded confusion or high fever and zero stated negatives under Rules A and D.
